**ECB launches Project Pontes to connect tokenised assets with central bank money**

*The initiative aims to build permanent infrastructure linking distributed ledger platforms to Eurosystem settlement, moving tokenisation from pilot to production.*

The European Central Bank has launched Project Pontes, a new programme designed to create interoperability between tokenised financial market platforms and central bank money settlement systems. The project follows a series of exploratory trials across the Eurosystem and represents a shift from experimentation to building durable infrastructure.

Pontes sits alongside the ECB's broader work on the digital euro and its existing market infrastructure, including TARGET and TIPS. Where earlier initiatives such as the ECB's distributed ledger technology (DLT) trials tested whether tokenised bonds and other instruments could settle against central bank liquidity, Pontes is intended to provide a standing framework for doing so at scale. The goal is to ensure that as European capital markets adopt tokenisation, settlement remains anchored in sovereign money rather than migrating to private stablecoins or other alternatives.

The project reinforces the Eurosystem's strategy of maintaining central bank relevance as financial market plumbing evolves. It also signals that European regulators see tokenised settlement not as a distant prospect but as something requiring production-grade infrastructure now. Banks and market infrastructure operators will need to assess how Pontes interacts with their own technology roadmaps.

*Sources: [ECB Launches Pontes to Drive Tokenization](https://www.financemagnates.com/cryptocurrency/ecb-launches-pontes-to-drive-tokenization/) — Finance Magnates*

**Riverty opens Luxembourg bank to scale European payments and consumer finance**

*The new banking licence gives the Bertelsmann-owned BNPL provider a platform to expand lending and payments across EU markets from a single regulated entity.*

Riverty has opened Riverty Bank S.A. in Luxembourg, establishing a fully licensed banking entity to underpin its European consumer finance and payments operations. The move gives the company, owned by Bertelsmann, a single regulatory base from which to passport services across the EU.

Riverty operates primarily in the buy-now-pay-later and invoicing space across several European markets including Germany, the Netherlands and Austria. Until now, its operations have relied on a patchwork of national licences and partnerships. A dedicated banking licence consolidates this, providing direct access to deposit-taking and lending capabilities that can support product expansion, particularly as BNPL regulation tightens across Europe.

The UK's Financial Conduct Authority published its final BNPL rules on February 11 in Policy Statement PS26/1, and the EU's revised Consumer Credit Directive already brings many BNPL products into scope. Riverty's choice of Luxembourg follows a well-established pattern among fintechs and payment firms seeking a flexible EU hub.

*Sources: [Riverty opens bank in Luxembourg](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110949/riverty-opens-bank-in-luxembourg?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**Ant International unveils AI-native product stack for global payments and treasury**

*The full-stack launch positions cross-border infrastructure as an integrated AI platform rather than a collection of standalone services.*

Ant International has launched what it describes as a full AI-native product stack covering payments, accounts, foreign exchange, treasury and growth operations for global businesses. The suite is designed to embed machine learning across each layer of cross-border financial operations rather than bolting AI capabilities onto existing workflows.

The release reflects a broader industry pattern in which infrastructure providers are repackaging their services around AI orchestration. Ant International, the overseas arm of Ant Group, already operates Alipay+ and processes cross-border transactions for merchants and financial institutions across Asia, Europe and the Middle East. Wrapping these capabilities in an AI-native framework is intended to improve transaction routing, FX optimisation and fraud detection simultaneously.

The competitive implication extends well beyond Asia. Ant's approach mirrors moves by Visa, Mastercard and Stripe to position AI not as an add-on but as the core operating layer. As agentic commerce gains traction, the providers that integrate AI most deeply into their payment and treasury stacks are likely to set the terms for how cross-border money movement evolves.

*Sources: [Ant International launches financial AI stack](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48436/ant-international-launches-financial-ai-stack?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
